text:
maria_support: Customer reports sudden billing spike + intermittent 403s when calling /v1/completions. Says they see 403 about ~1/10 requests and gets different request ids each time. Need minimal repro + request ids + debug bundle.
ryan_oncall: can you ask for the exact request-id header from the failing requests (x-request-id or x-redwood-request-id). also need the customer region and whether they use our hosted api or dedicated.
maria_support: pulled a snippet from customer chat: "Response 403, body: {\"error\":\"Forbidden\"}, headers: x-request-id: 01FZ9X2K..." — they sent three different request ids. they’re on hosted (us-west). ticket 78921 started.
thomas_sdk: quick repro checklist for customer to run: 1) curl -v to capture headers 2) minimal python/js/go examples (I’ll paste below) 3) attach support-bundle. keep it tiny to reduce noise.
ryan_oncall: paste this curl for them to run (copy/paste):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"test"}' \ 
  -v
```
ryan_oncall: the -i and -v will print response headers; ask them to paste the full headers and the exact x-request-id values. if they get 403 include the raw response body.
maria_support: customer already ran a curl but didn’t include headers; asked them to rerun and paste.
thomas_sdk: minimal python repro (requests) to share:
```python
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions'
headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
payload = {'model': 'redwood-1.0', 'input': 'hi'}

resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print('status', resp.status_code)
print('x-request-id', resp.headers.get('x-request-id'))
print(resp.text)
```
thomas_sdk: minimal node (node 18+) repro:
```js
import fetch from 'node-fetch'
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'hello'})
})
console.log('status', res.status)
console.log('x-request-id', res.headers.get('x-request-id'))
console.log(await res.text())
```
thomas_sdk: minimal go repro:
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main() {
  apiKey := os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  reqBody := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"hello"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewBuffer(reqBody))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("err", err); return }
  defer resp.Body.Close()
  fmt.Println("status", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("x-request-id", resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"))
}
```
anya_infra: to collect a debug bundle from the hosted side, tell the customer to run our support-bundle helper (if they’re comfortable) or we can collect from server side once they give request ids and approximate timestamps. sample command we ask them to run locally to collect client-side traces:
```
# collect minimal client logs + http traces
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
mkdir -p /tmp/redwood-debug && 
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"trace"}' 2>&1 | tee /tmp/redwood-debug/curl-$(date +%s).log
```
anya_infra: if they can’t run that, ask for the timestamp window (UTC) and the x-request-id(s) and I’ll pull host-side logs: `support-infra logs fetch --since "2026-03-17T09:50:00Z" --until "2026-03-17T10:10:00Z" --filter-ids 01FZ...`
ryan_oncall: a few quick debugging tips: 1) ask if they rotate API keys or use proxy; 2) check any intermediate networking proxies that could strip auth headers; 3) confirm there’s no rate limiting on their account causing 403s (we can verify on our side).
maria_support: I’ve asked customer to rerun curl + python snippet and paste headers + body and attach logs. asked for region and whether they’re behind a proxy.
support-bot: Ticket 78921 created and linked to this thread. Agent ryan_oncall assigned.
ryan_oncall: once they paste the x-request-ids I’ll pull the server logs and share findings here. if we see 403 from our auth service we’ll escalate to eng-sre with the ids and timestamps.
maria_support: thanks — I’ll update ticket with their replies when they come in. :thumbsup:
